sections.en: 1 ἀκαταστασία; cf. Catal., l. c., 7, the whole year varied. and winds will blow etc. : same words Geopon., p. 28, 4. 2 ἐπιχείσθαι M. 3 After ἀνεπιτήδειον a lacuna of almost twenty letters is indicated in the codd. τὸ ἀκρόδρυα A. 4 I transcribed A(ngelicum); I collated M(ediolanensem) f. 99. 6 τρεῖς omitted A. 9 γάλοι A. 10 ἤτοι ζ′ ἥμισυ secluded. μαλίναι A : μαλίναι with γ superscribed M = malignae. 12 λιδοῦναι new word perhaps corrupted from d(ies) idoneae. 13 δὲ omitted A. 15 ὑπὸ γῆν καὶ ὑπὲρ γῆν M. 16 I edited from the Ambrosian codex B 38 sup. (= Mediolanensis 8), f. 108, a copy of which Dominicus Bassi kindly sent me : the Angelicus itself from which that Ambrosianus seems to have been copied, I was not given the opportunity to use. 18 δισσωμένω cod. 19 στερεῷ Δα cod.

1 De hac Gallorum computandi ratione, cf. Revue des études anciennes, IV, 1902, p. 290 s., ubi hic Palchi locus iam publici iuris factus est.
2 Fortasse Serapio Antiochenus qui in Hipparchi geographiam commentaria scripsit, cf. Byz. Zeitschr., VIII, 1899, p. 525. — Eiusdem nonnulla excerpta in Catal., I, p. 99, 101 edidimus.
sections.en:
1 On this method of computing of the Gauls, cf. Revue des études anciennes, IV, 1902, p. 290 f., where this passage of Palchus has already been made public.
2 Perhaps Serapio of Antioch who wrote commentaries on the geography of Hipparchus, cf. Byz. Zeitschr., VIII, 1899, p. 525. — We have edited some excerpts of the same in Catal., I, p. 99, 101.

summary.headline: Inceptions and Lunar Days
summary.text: Astrological instructions from chapter 6 on inceptions: observe the ascendant’s decan, lunar novenaries, Roman calendar days, and the lunar periods called malinai and lidounai, when actions should be avoided or undertaken. A section on contracts with women, attributed to Serapion, gives conditions involving the Moon, Venus, Jupiter, the Sun, signs, houses, trines, and malefics; the opening also predicts unstable weather and poor planting conditions.
